DESIGN REVISION — captured Giles's corrections, plan updated (supersedes the phase detail above)

Giles reviewed the proposal and gave three corrections that reshape the design. Locked version:

1. QC IS NOT a universal gate.
   QC is only performed on BESPOKE components. For standard/consumable parts there is no QC step — completion of the goods-in IS the evidence that the quantity of parts arrived. So there is no mandatory QC tick on general goods-in; the checklist/state model must only expect QC on bespoke/built parts, and for everything else 'arrived + task closed' = arrival proof.

2. NO filtering of the evidence — rolling 60-day view against the FIXED baseline.
   Do not filter or re-categorise the evidence. Instead surface a ROLLING 60-day window of items flagged with the tag, and benchmark that window against the ORIGINAL issue-category breakdown (the 9 categories / 564-flag historical state) held as a hard, fixed baseline. The baseline is the benchmark we track improvement against; the rolling window shows the recent delta. Trend over the fixed benchmark, not a filtered subset.

3. The weekly capture loop / focus task (the recurring mechanism).
   - The loop reviews WHAT HAPPENED in the rolling 60-day window and ASSESSES it against the benchmark.
   - Every MONDAY it surfaces ONE task assigned to RICHARD at purchasing@sesameaccess.com, DUE DATE = today (the Monday), giving him the week's focus.
   - Task project = Richard / Giles 1:1 (GID 1204237507645072). This is the weekly 1:1 project (sections: Discussion topics, FYIs, Project updates, Action items) — so the Monday task is the standing weekly-review prompt feeding the 1:1.
   - Section recommendation: Action items (the working/owned section), but confirm if Giles wants it under Discussion topics instead.

Net effect on the plan: Change C (hard-block premature completion) stays OUT. The Stock State field stays but only as visibility + only bespoke parts carry a QC expectation. The dashboard/report become the rolling-60-day-vs-fixed-baseline view. And the recurring output is the Monday 1:1 focus task to Richard.

To lock and implement I need:
A. Confirm the Monday task section (Action items recommended) + the task naming/wording you want (I'll draft one).
B. Confirm the fixed baseline = the original 9-category breakdown from the 2026-08-13 assessment (I'll hold it as the benchmark table).
C. Confirm Richard's Asana assignee is matched via purchasing@sesameaccess.com (that's the mailbox identity — I'll assign by the user that maps to it).

Once A-C are confirmed I'll build: (1) the rolling-60-day flag pull, (2) the benchmark comparison, (3) the Monday cron that creates the Richard 1:1 focus task assigned + due-today in project 1204237507645072.
